docs.title: Digital Waste Tracking API
docs.text:
Digital Waste Tracking (DWT) is a UK cross-government programme to build a single digital service for tracking waste movements, ultimately replacing paper-based waste transfer notes (WTNs). Its main aims are to reduce waste crime and misclassification, improve data on how waste moves domestically to support the transition to a circular economy, and cut the administrative burden of the current fragmented, paper-based system.

To support this service, the DWT team is developing an API which will integrate with third-party solutions to create an optimised service that works for all parties, including producers, brokers, carriers/drivers and receivers of waste.

This hub includes all the current documentation relating to the API development project for software providers. It will be updated on a regular basis as the service develops.

docs.title: Current status:
docs.text:
The first 'development milestone' of the service was Beta-1, completed in Sep/Oct 2026. This rollout tested basic API interactions in a sandbox environment to ensure proof of concept and identify potential issues.

The team is currently focused on Beta-2, with key input from software providers across a range of journey scenarios to further develop and refine the service.

docs.title: Waste movement delivery events
docs.text:
The API will support all four significant events in the waste movement cycle:

  • Arrange movement of waste (creation)
  • Collection of waste (collection)
  • Delivery of waste (delivery)
  • Receipt of waste (receipt)

docs.title: Digital Waste Tracking API: journey scenarios - Beta 2
docs.text:
The Digital Waste Tracking API will enable a variety of journey scenarios which will be rolled out through the various Beta incarnations. Beta 2 adds new journeys to the original journeys in Beta 1 and will be the first release of the DWT API where you can record a waste movement from start to finish, with full input validation on every request.

A reminder of our original DWT API integration guidance

docs.title: B1A - Single non-hazardous movement
docs.text:
A waste movement is made up of 4 events:

  1. Create the movement with POST /movements. This returns a Movement ID.
  2. Record the collection with POST /movements/{movementId}/collection.
  3. Record the delivery with POST /deliveries. This returns a Delivery ID.
  4. Record the receipt with POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

You need a valid Movement ID to record a collection or a delivery.

docs.title: B1B - Several non-hazardous movements delivered together
docs.text:
You can deliver several non-hazardous movements to a receiving site in one delivery. To do this, list all their Movement IDs when you call POST /deliveries. This returns one new Delivery ID for the whole group.

The receiving site uses this Delivery ID to record the receipt, using POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

docs.title: B1C - Waste delivered to more than one receiving site
docs.text: Waste from one or more movements can be split between more than one receiving site. List the Movement IDs when you call POST /deliveries. Each receiving site then records its own receipt against the Delivery ID, using POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

docs.title: B1D - Waste received without a Delivery ID
docs.text: A receiving site can accept waste that arrives without a Delivery ID. Record the receipt with POST /receipts, and explain why there’s no Delivery ID in reasonForNoDeliveryId. This returns a new Delivery ID for the receipt.

docs.title: B2A - Hazardous movement
docs.text:
A movement is hazardous if any of its waste items has a hazardous European Waste Catalogue (EWC) code when you create it with POST /movements. It stays hazardous for all 4 events.

When you record the delivery, POST /deliveries still returns a Delivery ID, however this is the same code as the initial Movement ID. Use it to record the receipt in the usual way.

docs.title: B2B - Hazardous and non-hazardous movements delivered together
docs.text:
You can include hazardous and non-hazardous movements in the same POST /deliveries request. The response gives you:

  • one new Delivery ID for all the non-hazardous movements together
  • one Delivery ID for each hazardous movement, which is the same as its initial Movement ID

Hazardous movements cannot be grouped with other hazardous movements for receipt.

docs.title: B2C - Linking related movements
docs.text:
Some jobs need more than one movement, for example when waste is removed over several trips.

To link these movements, add the same reference to each one when you create it with POST /movements.

docs.title: Receipt of waste: receiver details reference guide
docs.text: This guide provides implementation and test guidance for the DWT receipt flow. It covers the receiver details captured with a receipt, not the full waste-movement data contract.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: When an authenticated user submits a receipt for transfer of waste, the receiving organisation and site must be identified accurately so regulators can attribute the receipt to the correct receiver and support the receiver's duty-of-care obligations.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before validating or creating the receipt, the receipt submitter must:

  • be authenticated
  • provide a valid API code
  • provide a valid Delivery ID

docs.title: Receiver information
docs.text:
The receipt must contain one receiver declaration. The declared receiver has the following information:

Information Requirement Site name Required. Authorisation number Required and must match a valid UK authorisation-number format. Reuse the existing isValidAuthorisationNumber validation based on the RoW codebase's existing expression rather than introducing a divergent rule. Receipt address Required. The postcode is required; the full address is optional under the shared address schema. Contact details At least one of email address or phone number is required. Either may be supplied on its own; both may also be supplied. Each value must be validated.

Receipt receiver details are not an array, and are therefore unlike receiver details at creation. Validation follows the shared address schema already used for the producer and broker/dealer (postcode required, UK postcode format; full address optional):

The example below shows one receiver object. It illustrates the data shape, not the endpoint's property name; use the approved receipt contract for that.

type ReceiverDetails = {
  siteName: string // required
  authorisationNumber: string // required; valid UK authorisation number format
  address: Address // required; postcode required, fullAddress optional
  contactDetails: ContactDetails // at least one contact method required
}

type ContactDetails = {
  // at least one of emailAddress / phoneNumber required; both allowed
  emailAddress?: string // standard email format
  phoneNumber?: string // valid phone number
}

docs.title: Validation and outcomes
docs.text:
Reject the receipt and return a useful field-level validation error when any of these conditions apply:

Condition Expected outcome No receiver is supplied Do not create the receipt; report that receiver details are required. More than one receiver is supplied Do not create the receipt; report that only one receiver is required. Site name is missing Do not create the receipt; report that a site name is required. Authorisation number is missing Do not create the receipt; report that an authorisation number is required. Authorisation number is malformed Do not create the receipt; report that the authorisation number is invalid. Receipt address or required postcode is missing Do not create the receipt; report that the receipt address is required. Postcode is invalid Do not create the receipt; report that the postcode is invalid. Both email address and phone number are missing Do not create the receipt; report that at least one contact method is required. A supplied email address is invalid Do not create the receipt; report that the email address is invalid. A supplied phone number is invalid Do not create the receipt; report that the phone number is invalid. All required receiver information is valid Create the receipt.

Use the existing validation envelope (D-039) and field-level errors keyed to the receiver field, in the form Receivers.<field>. Match the exact casing and property names to the approved endpoint schema and existing API error conventions.

UK postcode is required, in standard format. This is acceptable even without a full postal address.

docs.title: Suggested implementation flow
docs.text:
1. Validate the receipt submitter's authentication, API code and Delivery ID using the existing receipt flow.
  2. Read the receiver declaration from the receipt request using the approved contract field and shape.
  3. Require exactly one actual receiver; reject a missing receiver or multiple receivers.
  4. Validate the site name, authorisation number, receipt address and postcode, and contact details.
  5. Reuse the existing authorisation-number, address, email and phone validators wherever available. Avoid duplicating validation rules in the receipt-specific code.
  6. If validation fails, return the standard validation envelope with actionable field-level errors and do not create a partial receipt.
  7. If validation succeeds, persist the receiver details as part of the receipt so the receiver can be identified in regulatory reporting.

docs.title: Acceptance-test checklist
docs.text:
• A valid receiver with valid site name, authorisation number, receipt address and contact details creates a receipt.
  • A receipt with more than one receiver is rejected with an explanation that only one is allowed.
  • A receiver with only a valid email address is accepted.
  • A receiver with only a valid phone number is accepted.
  • A receiver with both a valid phone number and a valid email is accepted.
  • Missing site name, authorisation number or receipt address is rejected with the corresponding field error.
  • Missing both contact methods is rejected; missing either one alone is accepted.
  • Invalid authorisation number, postcode, email address and phone number are each rejected with the corresponding field error.
  • Authentication, API code and Delivery ID preconditions are covered by the existing receipt-flow tests.
  • Validation errors use the existing envelope and identify the invalid receiver field.
  • Missing UK postcode or invalid UK postcode format is rejected.
  • No receipt is persisted on any validation failure.

docs.title: Data protection and non-functional impact
docs.text: The ticket records no additional non-functional impact beyond standard conformance. It also says receiver contact details are already collected at receipt in production, so this change does not introduce a new category of personal data or require additional data-protection work according to the story.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
• DWTC-233: Receipt - Reporting the receiver details
  • Software Journey View

docs.title: Questions for stakeholders
docs.text:
The current receipt schema in the beta-2 API specification differs from details in DWTC-233 and this guide. Please confirm the intended requirements before we align the API documentation:

  • Receiver field name and shape: Should the request use the current schema's single receiverSite object, or a different receiver property and shape?
  • Contact details: Should email address and phone number be nested inside contactDetails, or remain top-level fields on receiverSite as in the current schema?
  • Postcode formats: Should the receipt accept UK postcodes only, as this guide states, or also Irish Eircodes as in the current address schema?
  • Full address: Is fullAddress optional, as this guide says, or required for a physical receipt site as in the current schema?
  • Validation error paths: Should field-level errors use Receivers.<field> as stated in DWTC-233, or use paths based on the current receiverSite field?

docs.title: Digital Waste Tracking API - Roadmap
docs.text:
Current status: The first 'development milestone' of the service was Beta-1, completed in Sep/Oct 2026. This rollout tested basic API interactions in a sandbox environment to ensure proof of concept and identify potential issues.

The team is currently focused on Beta-2, with key input from software providers across a range of journey scenarios to further develop and refine the service.

docs.title: Beta-1: Contract API test
docs.text:
Earliest integrated service - Sep/Oct 2026

All POST endpoints made available, with only validation against the payload structure, no individual data item validation.

Ability to map identifiers and events to new or existing entities in your system.

  1. Acknowledge waste movement
  2. Acknowledge collection using Movement ID
  3. Acknowledge delivery (incl. array of Movement IDs)
  4. Acknowledge receipt using Delivery ID

docs.title: Beta-2: Create end-to-end waste movement
docs.text:
Earliest testable service - Oct/Nov 2026

All POST endpoints amended to include full validation and conditionality against individual data items.

Ability to map data points to the DWT schema and design for curated scenarios and validation messages.

  1. Report a waste movement
  2. Report a collection using Movement ID
  3. Report a delivery (incl. array of Movement IDs)
  4. Report a receipt using Delivery ID

docs.title: Beta-3: Update, retrieve and reject
docs.text:
Earliest usable service - Nov/Dec 2026

All PUT and GET endpoints made available.

Ability to design amendment and retrieval processes in your system.

  1. Report a waste movement - UPDATE
  2. Report a collection using Movement ID - UPDATE
  3. Report a delivery (incl. array of Movement IDs) - REPORT A REJECTION
  4. Report a receipt using Delivery ID - UPDATE - REPORT A REJECTION

docs.title: Beta-4: Final iterations
docs.text:
Production-ready API - Jan 2027

Any final iterations and feedback that could not be deployed previously.

  1. Report a waste movement - UPDATE
  2. Report a collection using Movement ID - UPDATE
  3. Report a delivery (incl. array of Movement IDs) - REPORT A REJECTION
  4. Report a receipt using Delivery ID - UPDATE - REPORT A REJECTION

docs.title: Digital Waste Tracking: API integration guidance
docs.text:
Status: draft outline, v1.0

Owner: Dave Oliver

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• 1. Introduction
  • 2. Service overview
  • 2.1 Lifecycle stages
  • 2.2 Actors
  • 2.3 Core identifiers
  • 3. API reference
  • 4. Business rules and data reconciliation
  • 4.1 Collection cardinality
  • 4.2 Movement-to-delivery cardinality
  • Appendix A: glossary
  • Appendix B: endpoint quick reference

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: This document provides guidance for software providers building producer, broker, carrier/driver or receiver-facing systems that will interact with Defra's dedicated API to record waste movements.

docs.title: 2.1 Lifecycle stages
docs.text:
The API is organised around four stages:

Stage What happens Creation Movement created; estimated details declared; Movement ID generated Collection Carrier/driver records the collection against a Movement ID Delivery Driver records delivery and declares the Movement ID in scope; Delivery ID generated Receipt Receiving site records acceptance of the waste against the Delivery ID

docs.title: 2.2 Actors
docs.text:
• Producer / Controller (EA term) – the organisation whose waste is being moved
  • Broker / Controller (EA term) – arranges the movement on behalf of a producer or receiver
  • Carrier / Transporter (EA term) – the organisation licensed to transport the waste; may operate through a Driver as the field-level user recording events in real time
  • Receiver – the site accepting the waste for treatment, disposal or recovery

docs.title: 2.3 Core identifiers
docs.text:
• Waste Movement ID – movementId is the primary record of an intended waste movement, created before the waste moves
  • Waste Delivery ID – deliveryId is the record created at delivery; a single Delivery ID can bundle one or more Movement IDs together

docs.title: 3. API reference
docs.text:
You can see the current API spec at: Digital Waste Tracking OpenAPI specification.

The spec will update with each milestone in the development process – expect some shapes to shift before go-live.

docs.title: 4.1 Collection cardinality
docs.text: One collection entry per physical collection event, even where loads are later combined at delivery.

docs.title: 4.2 Movement-to-delivery cardinality
docs.text: Many Movement IDs can be linked to a single Delivery ID at delivery; a Delivery ID always originates from exactly one delivery event.

docs.title: Appendix A: glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning DWT Digital Waste Tracking – the digital service this API supports EA Environment Agency EWC European Waste Catalogue – the code list used to classify waste type HWCN Hazardous Waste Consignment Note – the paper record DWT replaces for hazardous waste POPs Persistent organic pollutants – chemicals subject to additional handling and reporting rules Waste Movement ID Identifier issued when a movement is created, before waste moves Waste Delivery ID Identifier issued at delivery; can link multiple Movement IDs together WTN Waste Transfer Note – the paper record DWT replaces for non-hazardous waste

docs.title: Appendix B: endpoint quick reference
docs.text: Method Path POST /movements POST /movements/{movementId}/collection POST /deliveries POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt

docs.title: OpenAPI specification — beta-1
docs.text: Endpoints for this version are served under the /beta-1 path prefix.

docs.title: OpenAPI specification — beta-2
docs.text: Endpoints for this version are served under the /beta-2 path prefix.

docs.title: Receipt of waste: journey scenarios - Beta 1
docs.text: The Digital Waste Tracking API will enable a variety of journey scenarios which will be rolled out through the various Beta incarnations. Beta 1 will include 4 journeys.

docs.title: B1A - Single non-hazardous movement
docs.text:
A waste movement is made up of 4 events:

  1. Create the movement with POST /movements. This returns a Movement ID.
  2. Record the collection with POST /movements/{movementId}/collection.
  3. Record the delivery with POST /deliveries. This returns a Delivery ID.
  4. Record the receipt with POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

You need a valid Movement ID to record a collection or a delivery.

docs.title: B1B - Several non-hazardous movements delivered together
docs.text:
You can deliver several non-hazardous movements to a receiving site in one delivery. To do this, list all their Movement IDs when you call POST /deliveries. This returns one new Delivery ID for the whole group.

The receiving site uses this Delivery ID to record the receipt, using POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

docs.title: B1C - Waste delivered to more than one receiving site
docs.text: Waste from one or more movements can be split between more than one receiving site. List the Movement IDs when you call POST /deliveries. Each receiving site then records its own receipt against the Delivery ID, using POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

docs.title: Digital Waste Tracking API: journey scenarios - Beta 3
docs.text: The Digital Waste Tracking API will enable a variety of journey scenarios which will be rolled out through the various Beta incarnations. Beta 3 adds new journeys to the journeys introduced in Beta 1 and Beta 2.

docs.title: B1A - Single non-hazardous movement
docs.text:
A waste movement is made up of 4 events:

  1. Create the movement with POST /movements. This returns a Movement ID.
  2. Record the collection with POST /movements/{movementId}/collection.
  3. Record the delivery with POST /deliveries. This returns a Delivery ID.
  4. Record the receipt with POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

You need a valid Movement ID to record a collection or a delivery.

docs.title: B1B - Several non-hazardous movements delivered together
docs.text:
You can deliver several non-hazardous movements to a receiving site in one delivery. To do this, list all their Movement IDs when you call POST /deliveries. This returns one new Delivery ID for the whole group.

The receiving site uses this Delivery ID to record the receipt, using POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

docs.title: B1C - Waste delivered to more than one receiving site
docs.text: Waste from one or more movements can be split between more than one receiving site. List the Movement IDs when you call POST /deliveries. Each receiving site then records its own receipt against the Delivery ID, using POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt.

docs.title: B1D - Waste received without a Delivery ID
docs.text: A receiving site can accept waste that arrives without a Delivery ID. Record the receipt with POST /receipts, and explain why there’s no Delivery ID in reasonForNoDeliveryId. This returns a new Delivery ID for the receipt.

docs.title: B2A - Hazardous movement
docs.text:
A movement is hazardous if any of its waste items has a hazardous European Waste Catalogue (EWC) code when you create it with POST /movements. It stays hazardous for all 4 events.

When you record the delivery, POST /deliveries still returns a Delivery ID, however this is the same code as the initial Movement ID. Use it to record the receipt in the usual way.

docs.title: B2B - Hazardous and non-hazardous movements delivered together
docs.text:
You can include hazardous and non-hazardous movements in the same POST /deliveries request. The response gives you:

  • one new Delivery ID for all the non-hazardous movements together
  • one Delivery ID for each hazardous movement, which is the same as its initial Movement ID

Hazardous movements cannot be grouped with other hazardous movements for receipt.

docs.title: B2C - Linking related movements
docs.text:
Some jobs need more than one movement, for example when waste is removed over several trips.

To link these movements, add the same reference to each one when you create it with POST /movements.

docs.title: B3A - Permitted updates
docs.text:
You can correct a movement, a collection or a receipt after you've recorded it. Use the PUT endpoint for that event:

  • PUT /movements/{movementId} to update the movement
  • PUT /movements/{movementId}/collection to update the collection
  • PUT /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt to update the receipt

Each update creates a new version of the event (V2). The original (V1) is kept, so there's a full history of what was submitted.

You cannot edit a delivery once you've recorded it. PUT /deliveries/{deliveryId} accepts only isDeleted. To correct a delivery, delete it and record a new one with POST /deliveries. You can only do this until a receipt has been recorded against it.

docs.title: B3B - Waste does not match its description at collection
docs.text:
Only the organisation that created a movement can change the description of its waste. You cannot change the waste description when you record a collection.

If the waste does not match its description, the carrier must tell the organisation that created the movement so they can update it.

docs.title: B3C - Movement with a handover from carrier to carrier
docs.text:
A movement can have more than one collection. This lets you record waste passing from one carrier to another before it’s delivered. Set collectionType when you call POST /movements/{movementId}/collection:

  • STATIC for a collection from a fixed location, such as the producer’s site
  • TRANSIT for a collection from another vehicle

The first collection must be STATIC. Every collection after that must be TRANSIT.

docs.title: Problem types
docs.text:
When a request to a beta endpoint of the Digital Waste Tracking API fails, the response body is an RFC 9457 Problem Details object with the content type application/problem+json.

Each problem has a type URI. The type URI identifies the kind of problem and links to one of the pages below.

Status Type Title 400 bad-request Bad Request 401 unauthorized Unauthorized 404 not-found Not Found 413 request-entity-too-large Request Entity Too Large 415 unsupported-media-type Unsupported Media Type 500 internal-server-error Internal Server Error

docs.title: Response members
docs.text: Member Always present Description type Yes URI of the problem type, for example https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/bad-request. Use this value, not title or detail, to decide how to handle the error. title Yes Short summary of the problem type. It is the same for every occurrence of that type. detail No Explanation of this occurrence. It is left out of 500 responses. Do not parse this text because it can change. instance Yes Path of the request that failed, for example /beta-1/movements. requestId Yes Trace ID for the request. It matches the x-request-id response header. Include it when you contact support. errors No Field-level validation errors. Only present on 400 responses caused by an invalid request body. See bad-request.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/problem+json
x-request-id: 4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f

{
  "type": "https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/not-found",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "detail": "No delivery exists with delivery ID: 25KMT4Z9",
  "instance": "/beta-1/deliveries/25KMT4Z9/receipt",
  "requestId": "4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f"
}

docs.title: Bad Request
docs.text:
Type https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/bad-request Title Bad Request Status 400

The request was rejected and nothing was stored. Correct the request before you send it again. Sending the same request again will fail in the same way.

docs.title: When this happens
docs.text: Cause Example detail errors present The request body does not match the endpoint's schema, for example a required field is missing or a value has the wrong type or format 2 validation errors occurred Yes beta-1 only: the apiCode in the body is not recognised. On beta-2 a missing or unrecognised API Code returns unauthorized. the API Code supplied is invalid No beta-2 only: the body still contains apiCode, which moved to the x-api-code header 1 validation error occurred (pointer /apiCode, NotAllowed) Yes A Movement ID in a POST /deliveries request does not exist No movement exists for movement ID(s): 25HRA0B2, 25HRA0B3 No The request body is not valid JSON Invalid request payload JSON format No The Authorization header is malformed Bad HTTP authentication header format No

docs.title: Validation errors
docs.text:
If the request body fails schema validation, the response includes an errors array with one entry for each problem found. All problems are reported together, so you can fix them in one go. A value of the wrong type — for example a string where an object is expected — is reported once, and nothing inside it is reported until its type is fixed.

Member Description message Human-readable description of the problem. pointer JSON Pointer to the field in the request body, for example /wasteItems/0/ewcCodes. errorType Category of the problem. One of the values in the table below. errorType Meaning NotProvided A required field is missing. NotAllowed A field is present that the endpoint does not accept. InvalidType A value has the wrong JSON type, for example a string instead of a number. InvalidFormat A value does not match the required format or pattern, for example a date. InvalidValue A value is not one of the allowed values. OutOfRange A value, string length or number of items is above the maximum or below the minimum. BusinessRuleViolation A value breaks a business rule. UnexpectedError Any other validation problem.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "type": "https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/bad-request",
  "title": "Bad Request",
  "detail": "2 validation errors occurred",
  "instance": "/beta-1/movements",
  "requestId": "4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "\"apiCode\" is required",
      "pointer": "/apiCode",
      "errorType": "NotProvided"
    },
    {
      "message": "must NOT have additional properties",
      "pointer": "/unknownField",
      "errorType": "NotAllowed"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: How to fix it
docs.text:
• Check each entry in errors and correct the field that pointer refers to.
  • Check the request against the spec for the version you are calling: beta-2 or beta-1.
  • On beta-2, send the apiCode in the x-api-code header, not in the body. On beta-1, check that the apiCode in the body is the one issued to your organisation.
  • For POST /deliveries, check that every Movement ID was returned by an earlier POST /movements request.

docs.title: Internal Server Error
docs.text:
Type https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/internal-server-error Title Internal Server Error Status 500

Something went wrong on our side and the request could not be completed. The problem is not caused by your request.

docs.title: When this happens
docs.text:
An unexpected error happened while the request was being processed, for example a database was temporarily unavailable.

These responses do not include a detail member, so that internal information is not exposed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "type": "https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/internal-server-error",
  "title": "Internal Server Error",
  "instance": "/beta-1/deliveries",
  "requestId": "4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f"
}

docs.title: How to fix it
docs.text:
• Wait a short time, then send the request again. Wait longer after each failed attempt.
  • If the problem continues, contact us and include the requestId and the time of the request.

docs.title: Not Found
docs.text:
Type https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/not-found Title Not Found Status 404

The resource in the request path does not exist, so nothing was stored.

docs.title: When this happens
docs.text: Cause Example detail The Movement ID in POST /movements/{movementId}/collection does not exist movementId not found The Delivery ID in POST /deliveries/{deliveryId}/receipt does not exist No delivery exists with delivery ID: 25KMT4Z9 The path or HTTP method does not match an endpoint Not Found

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "type": "https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/not-found",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "detail": "movementId not found",
  "instance": "/beta-1/movements/25HRA0B2/collection",
  "requestId": "4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f"
}

docs.title: How to fix it
docs.text:
• Check that the ID in the path is exactly the one the API returned. For example, use the movementId from POST /movements or the deliveryId from POST /deliveries.
  • Check that you are sending the request to the same environment that created the ID.
  • Check the path, API version prefix (for example /beta-1) and HTTP method against the API spec for the version you are calling: beta-2 or beta-1.

docs.title: Request Entity Too Large
docs.text:
Type https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/request-entity-too-large Title Request Entity Too Large Status 413

The request body is bigger than the maximum size allowed, so it was not processed.

docs.title: When this happens
docs.text: The request body is larger than 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "type": "https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/request-entity-too-large",
  "title": "Request Entity Too Large",
  "detail": "Payload content length greater than maximum allowed: 1048576",
  "instance": "/beta-1/receipts",
  "requestId": "4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f"
}

docs.title: How to fix it
docs.text:
• Split the data across several smaller requests.
  • Remove fields that are not needed. Fields the endpoint does not accept will be rejected anyway, see bad-request.

docs.title: Unauthorized
docs.text:
Type https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/unauthorized Title Unauthorized Status 401

The request did not include valid credentials, so it was not processed and nothing was stored.

docs.title: When this happens
docs.text:
Every request needs an access token. From beta-2 it also needs your organisation's API Code in a header.

Cause Applies to Example detail The Authorization header is missing All versions — The access token is invalid, has expired, or does not carry the waste-movement-external-api-resource-srv/access scope All versions — The x-api-code header is missing beta-2 The x-api-code header is required The x-api-code header holds an API Code that is unknown or has been disabled beta-2 The x-api-code header does not contain a valid API code

On beta-1, the API Code is sent in the request body instead; an unrecognised one returns a bad-request problem.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "type": "https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/unauthorized",
  "title": "Unauthorized",
  "detail": "The x-api-code header is required",
  "instance": "/beta-2/movements",
  "requestId": "4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f"
}

docs.title: How to fix it
docs.text:
• Get an access token with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant, using the client ID and secret you were given, and send it with every request as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • Request a new token when the current one expires.
  • Check that you are using the credentials for the right environment.
  • On beta-2, send your organisation's API Code with every request as x-api-code: <apiCode>, not in the body. API Codes are managed in the Waste Tracking Service; a disabled code is rejected.
  • If your credentials have stopped working, contact us and include the requestId.

An Authorization header that cannot be read returns a bad-request problem instead.

docs.title: Unsupported Media Type
docs.text:
Type https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/unsupported-media-type Title Unsupported Media Type Status 415

The request body is in a format the API does not accept, so it was not processed.

docs.title: When this happens
docs.text: The Content-Type header of the request is not a supported JSON type, for example application/xml.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "type": "https://defra.github.io/digital-waste-tracking-api-site/preview/problems/unsupported-media-type",
  "title": "Unsupported Media Type",
  "detail": "Unsupported Media Type",
  "instance": "/beta-1/movements",
  "requestId": "4f6c1f0e9a3b4c2d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f"
}

docs.title: How to fix it
docs.text: Send the request body as JSON with the header Content-Type: application/json.
